appraisal_events.evidence: « au haussement d'épaules que fit Gilberte en ôtant ses affaires » ; « une conversation ponctuée de silences et de monosyllabes » ; « Naturellement, vous vous trouvez gentil ! », me dit-elle en riant longuement ; « je sais que vous êtes fou de moi, mais cela ne me fait ni chaud ni froid, car je me fiche de vous ».
appraisal_events.explanation: Across the final visit Gilberte withholds herself from the narrator — shrug, sullen face, monosyllables, and a long laugh he can only read as indifference — and the passage closes on his decision to stop seeing her, so the local movement is a sustained, narrator-endorsed withdrawal of regard that leaves him powerless.

appraisal_events.evidence: « Puis redevenant Odette, elle se mit à parler anglais à sa fille » ; « ce fut comme si un mur m'avait caché une partie de la vie de Gilberte, comme si un génie malfaisant avait emmené loin de moi mon amie » ; « me faisait aussi délaissé et seul qu'un enlèvement » ; « sa mère avait involontairement accéléré l'évolution ».
appraisal_events.explanation: Odette's intervention, though explicitly well-meant toward the narrator, shuts him out: switching to English walls off Gilberte's life two steps away from him, and the narration names her as the involuntary accelerator of his loss.

status_effects.explanation: His secured happiness collapses into helpless suffering: he can neither reach Gilberte's meaning nor control his own coldness, and he ends by resolving to give her up.
He is left outside the closed palace of the English conversation and outside the dance party, excluded from the shared space of Gilberte's life while physically present in the room.
She gains clear leverage: her indifference sets the terms, her refusal to explain leaves him begging, and he must guess at a plane of her thought he cannot reach.

The same withdrawal strips her of charm in the narration — a livid, ravaged, monotonous face likened to a dull beach under an unchanging horizon — so her local attractiveness falls even as her power rises.

The narration lightly lowers her: her sensible maxim is credited to a wisdom borrowed from elsewhere, and the moment she is 'Odette again' she becomes the maleficent agent who carries her daughter away from him.

ambiguities: Gilberte's contemptuous meaning is the narrator's own translation of her laugh, which he immediately disowns (« le rire n'est pas un langage assez déterminé ») while her spoken words stay affectionate; the snub is secured by her conduct (shrug, silences, refusal to explain) rather than by the imputed contempt.
